qualifying_findings.title: Aix-DB ChatBI common-agent command execution
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record with VulnCheck disclosure reference
qualifying_findings.security_fact: Aix-DB 1.2.4 lets an authenticated non-admin send crafted chat input or a document through the ChatBI common agent's ungated deepagents execute tool to run host commands and expose datasource credentials or model API keys.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Aix-DB 1.2.4; POST /dify/get_answer and document-processing paths that reach the common-agent execute tool.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: No fixed version is stated in the collected record; restrict the endpoint and reconcile a maintainer fix before operational guidance.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It crosses the agent-to-host execution boundary from untrusted prompt or document content and can expose AI service credentials.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad Aix-DB and agent-tool catalog coverage; this repository retains the prompt/document-to-command-execution security boundary.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High that NVD records the in-window disclosure and stated impact; medium on remediation because no upstream maintainer patch was located.
follow_up_actions: Reconcile against the project maintainer's release history and verify any fixed version before synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway OAuth registration SSRF
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record referencing IBM PSIRT advisory
qualifying_findings.security_fact: Authenticated gateway creators can set oauth_config.token_url to make ContextForge POST OAuth client credentials to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or localhost; a portion of an unparsable response is reflected in the error.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway 0.1.0 through 1.0.5; OAuth-enabled gateway registration.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Apply IBM's advisory guidance; constrain OAuth token endpoints to an allowlist and block metadata and internal address ranges.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An MCP gateway is an agent tool-control boundary; SSRF can turn delegated gateway administration into internal-service access or credential exposure.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns the broad ContextForge/MCP entity; this repository owns the SSRF and delegated-authority implication.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High; NVD provides exact versions and links IBM's PSIRT source.
follow_up_actions: Fetch IBM's advisory during ingest to capture its exact fixed-release and remediation wording.

qualifying_findings.title: MCP TypeScript SDK experimental task cross-session access
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Security Advisory and NVD CVE record
qualifying_findings.security_fact: The experimental taskStore did not bind tasks to their creating session, so clients sharing an InMemoryTaskStore could list, read, or cancel one another's tasks.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.24.0 through 1.31.0 when an HTTP server passes taskStore to McpServer or Server; 2.x is not affected.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to 1.32.0 or later; preferably stop using deprecated experimental tasks. A temporary alternative is removing taskStore or using one store per session.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP task state can represent delegated agent work. Cross-session access breaks tenant, confidentiality, integrity, and cancellation boundaries.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns the broad MCP SDK entity; this repository retains the session-isolation security finding.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High; the maintainer-published GitHub advisory states scope, mitigations, and patched version.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, check whether existing MCP SDK leaves can receive this as a distinct task-state isolation boundary.

qualifying_findings.title: djust MCP template-path readability oracle
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD record referencing GitHub advisory, patches, and releases
qualifying_findings.security_fact: The find_handlers_for_template MCP tool accepts a readable absolute path outside the configured template directories, exposing file existence/readability and matching snippets through the local stdio MCP server.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: djust 0.9.0 until 1.0.10, 1.1.7, 1.2.4, and 1.3.0rc8; local MCP clients running as the same operating-system user.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It shows that an ostensibly local agent tool must still enforce a workspace/path capability boundary rather than trust every same-user client.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns the broad djust and MCP entity coverage; this repository keeps the local-tool file-boundary analysis.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for scope and fixes from NVD's linked maintainer references; low severity should be retained as context, not inflated.
follow_up_actions: Verify the advisory's local-only preconditions during synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: Trigger.dev CLI MCP server missing authentication
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record referencing project GitHub advisory
qualifying_findings.security_fact: trigger dev --mcp binds all interfaces without authentication and exposes MCP SSE/messages endpoints, allowing a LAN attacker or malicious webpage to invoke run-management tools using the developer's stored access token.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: trigger.dev cli-v3 3.0.0 before 4.5.4; developer workstations with the MCP server exposed beyond loopback.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to 4.5.4 or later and keep development MCP endpoints restricted to trusted local/network boundaries.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An unauthenticated browser or LAN request can exercise an agent-tool surface with the developer's existing delegated authority.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns the broad Trigger.dev entity; this repository retains the local MCP exposure and authority-escalation implication.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for the affected range and action surface in NVD; reconfirm project advisory content during ingest.
follow_up_actions: Confirm whether the CLI's patch changes listener binding, authentication, or both.

qualifying_findings.title: Red Hat OpenShift AI evaluation-job model URL secret exposure
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record and Red Hat security-advisory index
qualifying_findings.security_fact: An authenticated user who can submit an lm-evaluation-harness job can provide a malicious model URL that makes the job disclose the tenant model-authentication secret to an external listener or SSRF reachable internal endpoints.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Red Hat OpenShift AI lm-evaluation-harness evaluation jobs; exact affected/fixed builds were not present in the collected NVD record.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Await the linked Red Hat erratum for fixed build details; meanwhile restrict model URLs to approved sources and isolate evaluation-job network egress and secrets.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Evaluation and release-gate infrastructure often holds model credentials; untrusted model provenance can turn that gate into an SSRF and secret-exfiltration path.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns general OpenShift AI and evaluation tooling coverage; this repository owns the security control boundary for evaluation-job secrets and egress.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High for the published NVD mechanism; medium for versions and patch status pending the product erratum.
follow_up_actions: Locate the product-specific Red Hat erratum before durable remediation guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: Pydantic AI Harness nested-tool limit bypass
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record; vendor release page located for follow-up
qualifying_findings.security_fact: Pydantic AI Harness before 0.59.0 does not apply UsageLimits.tool_calls_limit to nested calls made through CodeMode run_code, allowing user or prompt-injected content to exceed a configured limit on costly or side-effecting tools.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Pydantic AI Harness before 0.59.0; nested run_code -> run_nested_call() tool dispatch.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to 0.59.0 or later and independently enforce budget and authorization limits at tool execution boundaries.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Prompt injection can amplify autonomous side effects or spend when a framework-level tool-call guard does not compose through nested execution.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns the broad Pydantic AI product entity; this repository retains the security implication for nested delegated tool authority.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium: NVD gives concrete version and mechanism, but the corresponding vendor advisory was not located in this run and version nomenclature needs reconciliation.
follow_up_actions: Verify the exact package/release lineage and primary maintainer advisory before synthesis.

qualifying_findings.title: D365 F&O MCP Server default empty API-key exposure
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD CVE record referencing GitHub advisory, commits, and v1.11.0 release
qualifying_findings.security_fact: The documented Azure deployment defaults API_KEY to empty while binding the HTTP MCP listener to 0.0.0.0, enabling unauthenticated calls to read/search tools and disclosure of indexed Dynamics 365 proprietary source snippets and security metadata when no other access control is configured.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: D365 F&O MCP Server before 1.11.0, specifically one-click Azure deployments left with an empty API key and without effective upstream authentication or network restriction.
qualifying_findings.mitigation_or_patch: Upgrade to 1.11.0, configure a non-empty API key, and enforce upstream authentication and network restrictions.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A read-only label does not make an agent data tool safe: default-deployed anonymous access can reveal code, privilege structure, and business metadata.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ai-wiki owns broad MCP server and product coverage; this repository retains the default-authentication and proprietary-data exposure security lens.
qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High; NVD states the deployment preconditions, impact, fixed version, and primary GitHub references.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, compare this with existing default-authentication MCP-server leaves to avoid duplicating the control pattern.
